title: Worksheet — Motion in a Straight Line (Class 12 NIOS Physics)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show every step in the subjective questions; choose one option for MCQs. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: The SI unit of acceleration is:
Distance is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.
questions.explanation: Path length ≥ straight-line distance between start and end.

questions.question: The third kinematic equation for uniform acceleration is v² = u² + ____.
questions.explanation: Eliminates time between v = u + at and s = ut + ½at².

questions.question: A car starts from rest with acceleration 3 m/s². Distance covered in 4 s:
A ball is dropped from rest and reaches the ground with velocity 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Height of drop:
A car decelerates uniformly from 25 m/s to rest in 10 s. Find the deceleration and the stopping distance.
questions.answer: Deceleration: a = (0 − 25)/10 = −2.5 m/s², so |a| = 2.5 m/s². Stopping distance: s = (u + v)/2 × t = (25 + 0)/2 × 10 = 125 m. (Or s = ut + ½at² = 250 − 125 = 125 m.)
questions.explanation: Apply v = u + at and the average-velocity formula.

questions.question: A stone is thrown upward at 25 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s². Find (i) maximum height, (ii) time of flight, (iii) velocity 1.5 s after launch.
questions.answer: (i) h_max = u²/(2g) = 625/20 = 31.25 m. (ii) t_total = 2u/g = 50/10 = 5 s. (iii) v = u − gt = 25 − 15 = 10 m/s, still upward.

questions.question: A v–t graph is straight from (0, 0) to (8, 16) m/s, then horizontal to (12, 16). Compute (i) acceleration in the first 8 s, (ii) total displacement after 12 s.
questions.answer: (i) a = (16 − 0)/(8 − 0) = 2 m/s². (ii) Total displacement = area under graph = triangle (½ × 8 × 16 = 64) + rectangle (4 × 16 = 64) = 128 m.
questions.explanation: Slope = a; area under v–t = displacement.

questions.question: (a) Derive the equation s = ut + (1/2) a t² from the definitions of velocity and acceleration. (b) A body moves with u = 5 m/s, a = 2 m/s². Compute s at t = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 s and tabulate.
questions.answer: (a) Average velocity = (u + v)/2; with v = u + at, average velocity = (u + u + at)/2 = u + (1/2)at. Displacement = average velocity × time = [u + (1/2)at] × t = ut + (1/2)at². (b) Tabulate using s = 5t + t²: t = 0 → s = 0; t = 1 → s = 6 m; t = 2 → s = 14 m; t = 3 → s = 24 m; t = 4 → s = 36 m.
questions.explanation: Standard derivation followed by a numerical table.

questions.question: (a) Sketch the v–t graph of a body that is dropped from rest, takes 3 s to fall, hits the ground and bounces back with no energy loss, then rises for 3 s before being caught at the original release height (take downward as positive, g = 10 m/s²). (b) Find the total distance and total displacement covered.
questions.answer: (a) Phase 1 (0–3 s, falling): straight line from (0, 0) to (3, 30) with slope +10. At t = 3 s, instantaneous bounce: v jumps from +30 to −30. Phase 2 (3–6 s, rising): straight line from (3, −30) to (6, 0) with slope +10. The graph has two segments meeting at the bounce, forming a 'V' shape mirrored about the t-axis. (b) Total distance: fall (h = ½ g t² = 45 m) + rise (45 m) = 90 m. Total displacement: starts at h = 0, ends at h = 0 → displacement = 0.
questions.explanation: Free-fall kinematics + symmetry; distance and displacement diverge here.
